From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Departures from Buyer Playbook and recommended pushback
**Status of source material:** Seller's draft and Disclosure Letter are the other side's documents and have been reviewed critically against our playbook only.

---

## 1. Threshold point: the "FINAL / agreed at principal level" framing

The Seller's preamble asserts that these positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams", are "marked FINAL" and "not intended to be re-opened". **We should not accept this characterisation.**

- Our playbook is explicit that the 20% cap and the 18-month claims period are fallbacks available **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. **No such authority has been given.** The Seller's statement that these were "settled" is therefore inconsistent with our instructions and should be treated as a negotiating assertion, not a fact.
- The "market context" paragraph (caps of 10–20%, 1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers as "standard") is advocacy, not a basis for us to move. Our positions are set by the playbook, not by the Seller's description of the market.
- Notably, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter at [11] states that "No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included." That undercuts the preamble's claim of a settled bargain.

**Recommendation:** Respond in writing that nothing in the Seller Update is agreed or "final" from the Buyer's side, that all points remain open, and that no fallback has been authorised. Ask the Seller to identify the basis (date, participants, document) for any claimed principal-level agreement so we can confirm with Amelia Frost that none exists.

---

## 2. Liability regime – departures and pushback

### 2.1 General warranty cap (cl. 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 opening; 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority (none given).
- **Action:** Mark up to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not concede the 20% figure. Do not describe 20% as acceptable in correspondence.

### 2.2 Thresholds (cl. 12.2)
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Analysis:** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours on both measures, and the switch from first-dollar ("tipping") to excess-only ("deductible") structure is a substantive economic shift – it effectively hands the Seller a AUD 250,000 free deductible on top of a high claim-by-claim hurdle. In a business with multiple identified medium-sized issues (Ironquay AUD 180,000 exposure, Sandbar AUD 330,000, DD-006), a AUD 25,000 de minimis could knock out a meaningful share of realistic claims.
- **Action:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar. Expressly state that Fundamental/Title claims and specific indemnities sit outside both thresholds.

### 2.3 Claims period (cl. 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general warranty claims, **and** a proposal that any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost approval (none given).
- **Analysis:** The second limb is the more dangerous one. A default rule that every limitation applies to every Claim unless carved out would silently sweep in Title, Tax, IP, payment covenants, specific indemnities and fraud. This is exactly the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook requires us to resist.
- **Action:** 24 months for general warranties. Delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" language and replace with the opposite default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated; each other category has its own regime.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title claims
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Analysis:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept a AUD 4,800,000 cap on a claim that we did not receive good title to the shares we paid AUD 24,000,000 for. This is a fundamental point and should be treated as non-negotiable.
- **Action:** Insist on a separate Fundamental/Title regime at 100% / six years minimum / no basket, de minimis or knowledge qualifier.

### 2.5 Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions "apply to all Claims of any nature".
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
- **Analysis:** As drafted, the Seller's language would attempt to cap and time-bar claims for the Seller's own fraud, and the non-reliance clause would attempt to bar misrepresentation claims arising from dishonest statements. This is unacceptable and in any event of doubtful enforceability; its presence in the draft is a red flag worth noting.
- **Action:** Insert an express, overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out that prevails over cl. 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5 and any exclusive-remedy provision. Confirm it cannot be waived.

### 2.6 Tax / IP
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime above".
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed; categories must remain separate.
- **Action:** State that Tax and IP are not settled and are not subsumed in the general regime. Do not propose numbers in this round – simply reserve position and require separate, specifically negotiated schedules.

---

## 3. Disclosure and knowledge

### 3.1 General disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2])
- **Seller:** Whole data room as at 22 September 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" are deemed disclosed.
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Analysis:** The Seller's own specific disclosures at items 2–10 show why this matters: the data room contains contractual provisions (Bluefen 11.2/11.3, Riverlark 8.1/9.2, Ironquay 7.3) whose consequences are not spelled out. Blanket data-room disclosure would allow the Seller to argue that any issue buried in a document was "disclosed" regardless of whether its significance was fairly identified. Public-register disclosure is even wider and unbounded by the data room.
- **Action:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2] as general disclosures. Replace with a fair-disclosure standard (disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter). Specific disclosures may cross-refer to data-room documents, but the document itself is not disclosure.
- Also address [1.4]: a "no admission" reservation is common, but it should not operate to deny that the matters listed are disclosed **against** specific warranties and nothing more. Ensure the Disclosure Letter is expressed to qualify only the identified warranties.

### 3.2 Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Analysis:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar extending to advisers and to anything "discoverable" – it would convert the Buyer's due diligence into a waiver of warranty protection and reverse the purpose of the warranties. Combined with whole-data-room disclosure, the Seller would have effectively no warranty exposure for anything in the data room.
- **Action:** Delete cl. 8.3. If any knowledge concept is to survive, it must be a Seller's-knowledge qualifier (actual knowledge of named individuals after due enquiry) attached to specific warranties, and it must not touch title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

---

## 4. Conditions and completion mechanics

### 4.1 Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours"; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter [2] admits **no** final written consent and **no** evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.
- **Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
- **Analysis:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%). The Seller's own disclosure confirms the condition is currently unsatisfied. A "satisfied on delivery" mechanism would let the Seller complete with a consent that is subject to unmet 11.3 conditions and therefore potentially ineffective.
- **Action:** Condition precedent: unconditional written consent under cl. 11.2 in agreed form, plus documentary evidence that each 11.3 condition has been satisfied (or irrevocably waived by Bluefen), delivered before Completion and satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably. Replace "reasonable endeavours" with an obligation to obtain, backed by a Buyer walk right / long-stop date.

### 4.2 Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release to be provided **following** Completion. Disclosure Letter [3] confirms not repaid and no final discharge in data room.
- **Playbook:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking **plus** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Analysis:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, completing with AUD 3,200,000 of secured bank debt still in place and only a promise of a later release is a direct conflict with the price basis. Clause 8.1 (change of control) also creates default risk on the share transfer itself.
- **Action:** Require (i) a payout letter from Riverlark as at the Completion date; (ii) repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow; (iii) executed deeds of release and PPSR/other discharges delivered at Completion. If the Seller insists on post-completion mechanics, that is only possible with Riverlark's irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt and Amelia Frost's express approval – neither currently exists, so our position is Completion-date release.

### 4.3 Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter [5] confirms absence from funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Analysis:** Saying it is "a matter for the Seller" is not the same as the Seller funding it. If the bonuses are triggered by Completion and paid by the Company post-Completion, the Buyer bears them. On-costs (superannuation, payroll tax) could be material on top of AUD 420,000 and are unquantified.
- **Action:** Insert a specific funds-flow line item for AUD 420,000 plus all superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs triggered, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion, with a Seller indemnity for any shortfall. Ask the Seller to quantify on-costs.

### 4.4 Title (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter [10] acknowledges this is simply the source relied on and that no Buyer verification is recorded.
- **Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Action:** Require ASIC company extract and current PPSR search (including confirming the Riverlark security is the only registered interest and will be discharged), Seller board approvals/authority evidence, and a Seller fundamental warranty on title backed by the separate regime in 2.4. Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient.

---

## 5. Specific risk items

### 5.1 Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1)
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way.
- **Analysis:** DD-004 cl. 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. If AUD 180,000 is unpaid, the Company may not own the relevant IP at Completion. An indemnity confined to the payment amount does not cover the real risk: loss or dispute over ownership, injunction, re-development, or third-party claims. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Action:** Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of title to or dispute over SOW3 (and any other Ironquay) Project Materials, including costs of obtaining a confirmatory assignment. Preserve the cure path: Seller to procure cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay before Completion; the AUD 180,000 figure to be verified against bank records and Ironquay confirmation rather than assumed either way.

### 5.2 Export/privacy incident (DD-006; cl. 4.6 / Sch. 6)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter [6]: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification obligation unknown; investigation preliminary; no loss amount stated.
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Analysis:** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the facts do not yet support – the Seller's own disclosure says the key questions are unanswered. Equally, we should not treat it as a confirmed breach. The point is that the matter is unresolved and the Seller is attempting to close it off by characterisation.
- **Action:** Delete the "not material" characterisation. Insert a pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and provide written updates (and the final report) to the Buyer before Completion; a bring-down disclosure obligation; and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident, outside the general cap/basket. Do not propose a price adjustment or quantum at this stage.

### 5.3 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011; AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** "Ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Analysis:** The Disclosure Letter [8] itself says the disclosure does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – so the Seller Update's "ordinary course" label goes beyond what the Seller has disclosed. Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each should be read together for timing and scope.
- **Action:** Request the renewal terms, notice/termination rights, invoicing and accrual status for each. Reserve position on treatment pending that information; do not accept the "ordinary course" label and do not currently assert Debt treatment or a price deduction.

### 5.4 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- Disclosure confirms a landlord notification obligation (not consent) and a Mossvale assignment restriction (not a change-of-control consent). These appear lower-risk on the current record but should be verified against the documents themselves, with a pre-Completion notification covenant for the lease and confirmation that Mossvale clause does not contain a separate change-of-control trigger.

---

## 6. Structural point – keep categories separate

Across the draft the Seller repeatedly folds everything into one regime: "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl. 13), limitations/non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5), Title "subject to the same caps", Tax/IP "settled under the general regime". These are facets of one strategy. Our mark-up should contain a single governing clause: the general cap, thresholds, time limit, knowledge and disclosure qualifiers apply **only** to general Warranty Claims; Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses), payment obligations and covenants each have their own stated regime; and fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct is excluded from all of them.

---

## 7. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "FINAL / agreed at principal level" | Asserted | Reject in writing; no Amelia Frost authority exists; all points open |
| 2 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; no fallback authorised |
| 3 | De minimis / basket | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess-only | AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first-dollar |
| 4 | Claims period | 18 months; limits apply to all Claims by default | 24 months; limits apply only to general warranties, expressly |
| 5 | Fundamental / Title | Same as general | Separate: 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge |
| 6 | Fraud / wilful concealment | Caught by all limits and non-reliance | Overriding, non-waivable carve-out from everything |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | Specific fair disclosure only; delete [1.1]/[1.2] |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3) | Blanket, includes advisers and "discoverable" matters | Delete; only Seller-knowledge qualifiers, never for title/capacity/fraud/indemnities |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | CP: unconditional consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met, pre-Completion |
| 10 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion |
| 11 | Bonuses (DD-005) | Not in funds flow | AUD 420k + on-costs as line item / Seller-funded; quantify on-costs |
| 12 | Title evidence | DD-012 register only | Independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence |
| 13 | Ironquay IP | Narrow SOW3 payment indemnity | Broaden to cover ownership risk; preserve cure; verify AUD 180k |
| 14 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Strike characterisation; preserve logs, investigate, updates, specific indemnity; no quantum assumed |
| 15 | Sandbar renewals | "Ordinary course" | Reserve; request terms; no Debt/price deduction asserted yet |
| 16 | Tax / IP | "Settled under general regime" | Expressly OPEN; separate schedules; no unlimited liability proposed |
| 17 | Category structure | Single override regime | Single clause keeping each category separate |

**Immediate next steps:** (a) confirm with Amelia Frost that no fallback or principal-level agreement has been given, so the response can state this unequivocally; (b) issue a written reply rejecting the "FINAL" framing and reserving all positions; (c) send a mark-up implementing items 2–17; (d) issue supplementary DD requests on Bluefen 11.3 evidence, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment/assignment, bonus on-costs, Sandbar renewal terms, and the DD-006 investigation status.

A default rule that every limitation applies to every Claim unless carved out would silently sweep in Title, Tax, IP, payment covenants, specific indemnities and fraud. This is exactly the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook requires us to resist.
- **Action:** 24 months for general warranties. Delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" language and replace with the opposite default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated; each other category has its own regime.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title claims
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Analysis:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept a AUD 4,800,000 cap on a claim that we did not receive good title to the shares we paid AUD 24,000,000 for. This is a fundamental point and should be treated as non-negotiable.
- **Action:** Insist on a separate Fundamental/Title regime at 100% / six years minimum / no basket, de minimis or knowledge qualifier.

### 2.5 Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions "apply to all Claims of any nature".
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
- **Analysis:** As drafted, the Seller's language would attempt to cap and time-bar claims for the Seller's own fraud, and the non-reliance clause would attempt to bar misrepresentation claims arising from dishonest statements. This is unacceptable and in any event of doubtful enforceability; its presence in the draft is a red flag worth noting.
- **Action:** Insert an express, overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out that prevails over cl. 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5 and any exclusive-remedy provision. Confirm it cannot be waived.

### 2.6 Tax / IP
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime above".
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed; categories must remain separate.
- **Action:** State that Tax and IP are not settled and are not subsumed in the general regime. Do not propose numbers in this round – simply reserve position and require separate, specifically negotiated schedules.

## 3. Disclosure and knowledge

### 3.1 General disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2])
- **Seller:** Whole data room as at 22 September 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" are deemed disclosed.
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Analysis:** The Seller's own specific disclosures at items 2–10 show why this matters: the data room contains contractual provisions (Bluefen 11.2/11.3, Riverlark 8.1/9.2, Ironquay 7.3) whose consequences are not spelled out. Blanket data-room disclosure would allow the Seller to argue that any issue buried in a document was "disclosed" regardless of whether its significance was fairly identified. Public-register disclosure is even wider and unbounded by the data room.
- **Action:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2] as general disclosures. Replace with a fair-disclosure standard (disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter). Specific disclosures may cross-refer to data-room documents, but the document itself is not disclosure.
- Also address [1.4]: a "no admission" reservation is common, but it should not operate to deny that the matters listed are disclosed **against** specific warranties and nothing more. Ensure the Disclosure Letter is expressed to qualify only the identified warranties.

### 3.2 Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Analysis:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar extending to advisers and to anything "discoverable" – it would convert the Buyer's due diligence into a waiver of warranty protection and reverse the purpose of the warranties. Combined with whole-data-room disclosure, the Seller would have effectively no warranty exposure for anything in the data room.
- **Action:** Delete cl. 8.3. If any knowledge concept is to survive, it must be a Seller's-knowledge qualifier (actual knowledge of named individuals after due enquiry) attached to specific warranties, and it must not touch title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

## 4. Conditions and completion mechanics

### 4.1 Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours"; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter [2] admits **no** final written consent and **no** evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.
- **Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
- **Analysis:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%). The Seller's own disclosure confirms the condition is currently unsatisfied. A "satisfied on delivery" mechanism would let the Seller complete with a consent that is subject to unmet 11.3 conditions and therefore potentially ineffective.
- **Action:** Condition precedent: unconditional written consent under cl. 11.2 in agreed form, plus documentary evidence that each 11.3 condition has been satisfied (or irrevocably waived by Bluefen), delivered before Completion and satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably. Replace "reasonable endeavours" with an obligation to obtain, backed by a Buyer walk right / long-stop date.

### 4.2 Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release to be provided **following** Completion. Disclosure Letter [3] confirms not repaid and no final discharge in data room.
- **Playbook:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking **plus** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Analysis:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, completing with AUD 3,200,000 of secured bank debt still in place and only a promise of a later release is a direct conflict with the price basis. Clause 8.1 (change of control) also creates default risk on the share transfer itself.
- **Action:** Require (i) a payout letter from Riverlark as at the Completion date; (ii) repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow; (iii) executed deeds of release and PPSR/other discharges delivered at Completion. If the Seller insists on post-completion mechanics, that is only possible with Riverlark's irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt and Amelia Frost's express approval – neither currently exists, so our position is Completion-date release.

### 4.3 Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter [5] confirms absence from funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Analysis:** Saying it is "a matter for the Seller" is not the same as the Seller funding it. If the bonuses are triggered by Completion and paid by the Company post-Completion, the Buyer bears them. On-costs (superannuation, payroll tax) could be material on top of AUD 420,000 and are unquantified.
- **Action:** Insert a specific funds-flow line item for AUD 420,000 plus all superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs triggered, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion, with a Seller indemnity for any shortfall. Ask the Seller to quantify on-costs.

### 4.4 Title (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter [10] acknowledges this is simply the source relied on and that no Buyer verification is recorded.
- **Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Action:** Require ASIC company extract and current PPSR search (including confirming the Riverlark security is the only registered interest and will be discharged), Seller board approvals/authority evidence, and a Seller fundamental warranty on title backed by the separate regime in 2.4. Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient.

## 5. Specific risk items

### 5.1 Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1)
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way.
- **Analysis:** DD-004 cl. 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. If AUD 180,000 is unpaid, the Company may not own the relevant IP at Completion. An indemnity confined to the payment amount does not cover the real risk: loss or dispute over ownership, injunction, re-development, or third-party claims. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Action:** Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of title to or dispute over SOW3 (and any other Ironquay) Project Materials, including costs of obtaining a confirmatory assignment. Preserve the cure path: Seller to procure cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay before Completion; the AUD 180,000 figure to be verified against bank records and Ironquay confirmation rather than assumed either way.

### 5.2 Export/privacy incident (DD-006; cl. 4.6 / Sch. 6)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter [6]: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification obligation unknown; investigation preliminary; no loss amount stated.
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Analysis:** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the facts do not yet support – the Seller's own disclosure says the key questions are unanswered. Equally, we should not treat it as a confirmed breach. The point is that the matter is unresolved and the Seller is attempting to close it off by characterisation.
- **Action:** Delete the "not material" characterisation. Insert a pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and provide written updates (and the final report) to the Buyer before Completion; a bring-down disclosure obligation; and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident, outside the general cap/basket. Do not propose a price adjustment or quantum at this stage.

### 5.3 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011; AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** "Ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Analysis:** The Disclosure Letter [8] itself says the disclosure does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – so the Seller Update's "ordinary course" label goes beyond what the Seller has disclosed. Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each should be read together for timing and scope.
- **Action:** Request the renewal terms, notice/termination rights, invoicing and accrual status for each. Reserve position on treatment pending that information; do not accept the "ordinary course" label and do not currently assert Debt treatment or a price deduction.

### 5.4 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- Disclosure confirms a landlord notification obligation (not consent) and a Mossvale assignment restriction (not a change-of-control consent). These appear lower-risk on the current record but should be verified against the documents themselves, with a pre-Completion notification covenant for the lease and confirmation that Mossvale clause does not contain a separate change-of-control trigger.

## 6. Structural point – keep categories separate

Across the draft the Seller repeatedly folds everything into one regime: "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl. 13), limitations/non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5), Title "subject to the same caps", Tax/IP "settled under the general regime". These are facets of one strategy. Our mark-up should contain a single governing clause: the general cap, thresholds, time limit, knowledge and disclosure qualifiers apply **only** to general Warranty Claims; Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses), payment obligations and covenants each have their own stated regime; and fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct is excluded from all of them.
